{{Quote|Sriluur is the source of every foul wind that blows through the galaxy.|Common smuggler's expression|<ref name="GATORWp" />}}
'''Sriluur''' was a [[Planet/Legends|planet]] in the [[Tharin sector/Legends|Tharin sector]] of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]]. [[Homeworld/Legends|Homeworld]] to the [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Weequay/Legends|Weequay]] [[Species/Legends|species]], Sriluur held a key position along the [[Sisar Run/Legends|Sisar Run]], one of the many important [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperlanes]] connecting [[Hutt Space/Legends|Hutt Space]] with the rest of the Outer Rim. The planet was [[Orbit/Legends|orbited]] by five [[Moon/Legends|moons]], most notably [[Ruul (moon)|Ruul]], the only one of the five able to support life. It was an arid world covered in [[Desert/Legends|deserts]], [[Volcano/Legends|volcanoes]] and [[Acid/Legends|acidic]] [[Ocean/Legends|seas]]. Despite this, the planet was almost entirely self-sufficient thanks to an unlikely but very productive agricultural sector. The planet had enormous reserves of [[Copper/Legends|copper]], but this resource went largely untapped by [[Mining/Legends|miners]]. Historically, the planet was part of Hutt Space, which meant [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] [[Crime lord/Legends|crime lords]] and representatives of the [[Black Sun/Legends|Black Sun]] criminal organization were a common sight on Sriluur.

The planet was colonized by a large group of [[Houk/Legends|Houk]] around [[282 BBY]], an event that was met with resentment from the Weequay. The ensuing [[Houk–Weequay conflicts]] lasted until the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], fearing growing [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggling]] and [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel]] tendencies, [[Subjugation of Sriluur|occupied]] the planet shortly before the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]]. Even though the Empire established a sizable military presence, crime continued to rise in the [[Sector/Legends|sector]]. Sriluur was invaded by the [[Yuuzhan Vong empire|Yuuzhan Vong Empire]] in [[26 ABY/Legends|26 ABY]], and its inhabitants were [[Slavery/Legends|enslaved]]. By [[137 ABY]], the world had been claimed by [[Darth Krayt]]'s [[Darth Krayt's Galactic Empire|Galactic Empire]].

==Description==
[[File:Sriluur_NEGAS.jpg|thumb|left|180px|Another view of Sriluur]]
Sriluur was an important [[Planet/Legends|world]] deep in the [[Kreetan Narrows]]<ref name="LoNH" /> along the [[Sisar Run/Legends|Sisar Run]] [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperlane]], which connected the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]] with some of the oldest portions of [[Hutt Space/Legends|Hutt Space]] through the [[Ac'fren Spur]] branch. The planet also served as a nexus for numerous other local trade routes, making it a popular destination for [[Merchant/Legends|traders]].<ref name="SSRp" /> Sriluur was orbited by five [[Moon/Legends|moons]]; of particular note was [[Ruul (moon)|Ruul]], a habitable world that was almost fully owned by the [[Weequay/Legends|Weequay]] [[Bulq family|Bulq clan]].<ref name="GATORWp" />

The dominant topographical features of Sriluur were white deserts, dry scrub-lands and rocky fields, and sandstorms were frequent.<ref name="SSRp" /> The planet had enormous [[Copper/Legends|copper]] reserves, but these were never exploited through large-scale [[Mining/Legends|mining]],<ref name="GATORWp" /> with miners instead preferring to focus on other metals,<ref name="GG12p" /> minerals and gems&mdash;exports vital to Sriluur's economy.<ref name="LECGp" /> Its [[Ocean/Legends|oceans]] were high in [[Acid/Legends|acid]] content,<ref name="GG12p" /> but still home to some lifeforms.<ref name="UAAp">''[[Ultimate Alien Anthology]]''</ref> Nearly all of the planet's northern hemisphere was covered by the [[Great Cueva Expanse]], an enormous desert consisting mainly of crater holes.<ref name="GG12p" /> The southern hemisphere, littered with dormant [[Volcano/Legends|volcanoes]] and black [[Transparisteel/Legends|transparisteel]] canyons, was home to most of the planet's inhabitants.<ref name="GATORWp" /> Despite the harsh environment, Sriluur was almost entirely self-sustaining, with an extensive agricultural sector centered around the [[Cupric Islands]].<ref name="GG12p" /> Clean water was a very valuable commodity on the planet, with most of the supply originating on nearby [[Sedri/Legends|Sedri]].<ref name="SSRp" /> The largest settlements on the arid world were the [[Meirm City]], the main trading port [[Dnalvec]], and the administrative center of [[Al-Campur]].<ref name="GATORWp" /> At the center of each Weequay [[City/Legends|city]] was a [[thal]], a black stone shrine to their gods.<ref name="NEGASp">''[[The New Essential Guide to Alien Species]]''</ref>

[[Politics/Legends|Politically]], Sriluur was under [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] hegemony for much of its history.<ref name="Atlasn1">Based on the planet's location on political maps throughout the ''[[The Essential Atlas]]''.</ref> While it maintained strong trade relations with the rest of Hutt Space, the Hutts never truly attempted to subjugate or conquer the planet, nor did they make efforts to [[Slavery/Legends|enslave]] the Weequay. The enormous criminal organization [[Black Sun/Legends|Black Sun]] was also heavily represented on Sriluur, but it was not until the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] [[Subjugation of Sriluur|seized control of the planet]] that it officially became part of a major political power.<ref name="GATORWp" />

Many non-[[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] predators were native to Sriluur.<ref name="UAAp" /> The [[bandigo]]s of [[Temptation Canyon]] were known for their distinctive howls, which many Weequay falsely attributed to "water nymphs"&mdash;the subject of at least one native myth. Bandigos hunted in packs of up to twenty individuals, and would often throw rocks at their prey. The [[Raquor'daan/Legends|dark wolves]], referred to as ''raquor'daan'' in Sriluurian, were stealthy canines who employed poison claws and a stinger tail to kill their prey. They were considered natural enemies of the bandigos, and as such were well respected by the Weequay,<ref name="GATORWp" /> who sometimes tamed the beasts to aid them in [[Hunting/Legends|hunting]].<ref name="TUR">''[[The Unknown Regions]]''</ref>

==History==
===Early history===
[[File:Dnalvec.jpg|thumb|left|250px|A settlement on Sriluur]]
The planet experienced an early period of intense tectonic activity, which was responsible for Sriluur's abundance of volcanoes. Its harsh, predator-ridden ecosystem originally forced the Weequay to roam the planet's deserts. Not until the [[Species/Legends|species]]' technology advanced to an industrial level<ref name="UAAp" /> some time before [[25,100 BBY]]<ref name="GATORWp" /> did they establish their first cities along the shores of Sriluur's acidic<ref name="GG12p" /> oceans. This development was vital to Weequay civilization, as the cities helped protect them from the planet's many predatory species, and gave them easier access to the bountiful seas.<ref name="UAAp" />

Sriluur remained undiscovered by [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] at large until around some point before 25,100 BBY. Even then, it was not frequently visited by other species aside from the occasional trader,<ref name="GATORWp" /> and managed to avoid the expansion of the [[Human/Legends|Human]] conqueror<ref name="XimH">{{SW|url=news/essential-atlas-extra-the-history-of-xim-and-the-tion-cluster|text=Essential Atlas Extra: The History of Xim and the Tion Cluster|int=Xim Week: The History of Xim and the Tion Cluster}}</ref> [[Xim/Legends|Xim's]] [[Xim's empire|empire]] during the last years of the [[Pre-Republic era]].<ref name="Atlasp">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> Weequay [[Mercenary/Legends|mercenaries]] were among the thousands of [[Troop/Legends|troops]] recruited by the [[Hutt Empire]] to combat Xim in the [[Xim Wars]].<ref name="XimDI" /> Following their victory in that war, the Hutts began pressing their interests on Sriluur,<ref name="GATORWp" /> to the extent that it was considered to be part of Hutt Space.<ref name="Atlasn1" /> The [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] did not discover the planet until somewhere between [[15,000 BBY/Legends|15,000]] and [[8000 BBY]].<ref name="Atlasp" /> The Weequay [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] went untouched by all major galactic conflicts<ref name="Atlasn2">Based on the planet's location on war maps throughout the ''[[The Essential Atlas]]''.</ref> up until the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]],<ref name="GATORWp" /> though Sriluur was the target of the six [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lords]] known as the [[Dread Masters]] during the [[Galactic War]] between the Republic and the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Sith Empire]]. As part of their conquest of sections of Hutt Space, the Dread Masters used [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] to induce a mass exodus from Sriluur, though it eventually fell back under the control of the Hutts.<ref name="Karagga">{{TORcite|type=operation|Karagga's Palace}}</ref>

===Houk colonization===
Thousands of [[Houk/Legends|Houk]] from the planet [[Lijuter]] colonized Sriluur in [[282 BBY]]. They established their settlement in what came to be known as the [[Houk Territories]] near Sriluur's equator,<ref name="GATORWp" /> not far from Dnalvec, though many chose to live in Weequay cities. Although far from the first non-native settlers on the planet, the Houk became regarded as cultural enemies by the Weequay. The ensuing [[Houk–Weequay conflicts]] would last for centuries, until, in approximately [[10 BBY/Legends|10 BBY]], all-out civil war erupted.<ref name="SSRp" /> Martial law in the Houk Territories was declared by the Weequay, while Houk militants attacked Weequay settlements. Several Weequay militias were formed, including the formidable [[Dnalvec Militia]].<ref name="GATORWp" /> The civil war ended when the Houk initiated a peace agreement,<ref name="GG12p" /> though minor hostilities between the factions continued until the Galactic Empire took control of the planet shortly before the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]].<ref name="GATORWp" />

===Travel advisory===
In [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]], prior to the start of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], the [[Nikto/Legends|Nikto]] [[Cult of M'dweshuu]]&mdash;a deadly religious sect from [[Kintan/Legends|Kintan]]&mdash;launched a series of homicidal attacks along the Sisar Run. At least twenty&ndash;seven individuals were killed by the M'dweshuu, and the [[Bureau of Ships and Services/Legends|Bureau of Ships and Services]] announced an advisory for the region. [[Dorosii]] the Hutt, the region's [[Appointed Intermediate]] to the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]] at the [[Time/Legends|time]], told the Republic that the local authorities could solve the cult violence without Republic interference, although the [[Jedi Council/Legends|Jedi Council]] was examining the situation. The string of attacks was later reported on by the [[HoloNet News/Legends|HoloNet News]].<ref name="HoloNet">{{HoloNetNewsWeb|45|regional/13228_1.html|Nikto Cultists Plague Sisar Run}}</ref>

===Galactic Civil War===
The Empire established a military presence on the planet, first and foremost to put an end to [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggling]] and [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel]] activity in the [[Sector/Legends|sector]],<ref name="GATORWp" /> but also as a hostile political gesture to the Hutts.<ref name="Atlasp" /> Garrisons were established along Sriluur's [[Copper Coast]], as well as in Meirm City,<ref name="AJ6">{{JournalCite|6|The Greel Wood Haven}}</ref> and the inexperienced [[Newen Streeg]] was installed as [[Governor/Legends|governor]] of the sector.<ref name="SSRp" /> Two [[Imperial-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Imperial''-class Star Destroyers]]&mdash;the [[Annihilator (Imperial I-class)|''Annihilator'']] and the ''[[Ruthless]]''&mdash;and one [[Strike-class medium cruiser|''Strike''-class medium cruiser]]&mdash;the ''[[Ion Storm]]''&mdash;were assigned to the area, but crime still flourished on Sriluur under Imperial rule. This was largely due to Imperial officials accepting bribes from Black Sun [[operative]]s. The Dnalvec Militia provided many recruits for the Alliance to Restore the Republic and various Hutt [[Crime lord/Legends|crime lords]] around this time. Sensing a problem, the Empire bombed most militia outposts in the area surrounding Dnalvec.<ref name="GATORWp" />

===Later history===
Following the defeat of the Black Sun leader [[Czethros]] during the [[Battle of Kessel (Black Sun Insurgency)|Battle of Kessel]] in [[24 ABY/Legends|24 ABY]],<ref name="YJK">''[[Young Jedi Knights: Crisis at Crystal Reef]]''</ref> the crime syndicate was all but disbanded, including its cells on Sriluur.<ref name="Leatherback">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/sw20020221a2|text=Last Call at Leatherback's|int=Last Call at Leatherback's}}</ref>

When the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]] broke out in [[25 ABY/Legends|25 ABY]],<ref name="NJOSBp" /> it was not long before [[Yuuzhan Vong]] [[Starship/Legends|spacecraft]] such as [[Yorik-et|coralskippers]] were [[Skirmish above Sriluur|spotted]] in vicinity of Sriluur.<ref name="AoCII">''[[The New Jedi Order: Agents of Chaos II: Jedi Eclipse]]''</ref> This led to a mass exodus of people who feared an imminent invasion of the planet. Many Weequay clans chose to stay behind and form militias to fight for their world. The Yuuzhan Vong-aligned [[Peace Brigade]] infiltrated Sriluur, harassing its inhabitants and attempting to rid the world of technology in preparation for the Yuuzhan Vong invasion.<ref name="Leatherback" /> When the Yuuzhan Vong finally [[Invasion of Sriluur|invaded]] in [[26 ABY/Legends|26 ABY]], the relatively low-tech defense put up by the natives was quickly overrun. The entire planet was conquered in a matter of days, and its inhabitants were enslaved.<ref name="NJOSBp" /> Even though their homeworld was [[Terraforming/Legends|terraformed]] by the occupants, the Weequay grudgingly adapted and continued to live on Sriluur after the war ended.<ref name="Atlasp" /> By [[137 ABY]], Sriluur was a subject world of [[Darth Krayt's Galactic Empire]].<ref name="LECGp" />

==Inhabitants==
[[File:Weequay-DC.png|thumb|250px|A Weequay male and female]]

===Weequay===
{{Main|Weequay/Legends}}
The planet's dominant species were the native Weequay, a technologically simple people.<ref name="UAAp" /> The species worshiped a pantheon of hundreds of gods, most of them inspired by natural forces and Sriluurian creatures.<ref name="GG12p" /> One example was [[Am-Shak/Legends|Am-Shak]], the god of thunder for whom the city of Al-Campur was named, as well as the moon god [[Quay]], the most important in the Weequay religion.<ref name="GATORWp" /> Weequay used a complex system of scents to communicate with members of their own clans; their [[Sriluurian]] [[Language/Legends|language]] was developed chiefly to facilitate communication with other clans and off-worlders.<ref name="UAAp" /> Traditional Weequay culture had no concept of individuality, rendering the idea of naming individuals alien to them. Typically, only those who chose to leave Sriluur took names.<ref name="NEGASp" /> These expatriates often found themselves working as mercenaries,<ref name="GG12p" /> and some, such as the [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]]'' [[Sora Bulq/Legends|Sora Bulq]]<ref name="NEGASp" /> and the pirate [[Hondo Ohnaka/Legends|Hondo Ohnaka]],<ref name="TCWEPG">''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars – The Official Episode Guide: Season 1]]''</ref> felt a large disconnect with Sriluur culture and religion.<ref name="NEGASp" />

===Immigrated species===
Sriluur was also home to a sizable population of Houk, a [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoid]] species that was noted for its great physical strength. A guiding principle in Houk culture was seeing violence as the preferable means to solve a conflict,<ref name="GG12p" /> which meant that they often found themselves at odds with the Weequay. Many Humans, Hutts, [[Nimbanel/Legends|Nimbanels]], and [[Toydarian/Legends|Toydarians]] were also present, though in far lesser numbers than the Houk.<ref name="GATORWp" />

==Locations==
===Al-Campur===
{{Main|Al-Campur}}
Al-Campur was the administrative center of Sriluur,<ref name="GATORWp" /> and home to a monastery devoted to Am-Shak, the Weequay god of thunder. The criminal underground of the city hosted several battle arenas. It was the capital of Sriluur for several years,<ref name="SWTSB" /> but was replaced by Meirm City in this capacity by 137 ABY.<ref name="LECGp" />

===Dnalvec===
{{Main|Dnalvec}}
Dnalvec was the main trading port of Sriluur, and home to three of the planet's four large-scale [[Spaceport/Legends|spaceports]]. It was also the site of the Bureau of Ships and Services office responsible for the entire Sisar Run hyperlane, and had the most Houk inhabitants of all the Weequay cities.<ref name="GATORWp" />

===Meirm City===
{{Main|Meirm City}}
The capital of Sriluur since approximately 137 ABY, Meirm City was situated along the shores of the copper-rich [[Meirm Sea]]. This proximity caused the city to constantly be covered in a layer of copper sand which, coupled with the constant acidic fog drifting in from the ocean, made erosion a big problem. The city was considered the heart of Weequay culture, and was littered with statues of the various Weequay gods,<ref name="GATORWp" /> especially Quay. Tension between the Houk and Weequay ensured it was a necessity to separate the city into distinct enclaves for each species.<ref name="SSRp" /> Meirm City was home to the [[Xizor Transport Systems/Legends|Xizor Transport Systems]]-owned [[Gricul Salvage Yards]], one of the best known repair yards in the Outer Rim.<ref name="GATORWp" />

==Behind the scenes==
Sriluur was first introduced by [[Craig Robert Carey]] in the article "[[The Greel Wood Haven]]" in [[Star Wars Adventure Journal 6|''Star Wars Adventure Journal'' 6]] ([[1995]]) as the homeworld of the Weequay species. The planet was substantially expanded upon in the [[roleplaying game]] sourcebooks ''[[Galaxy Guide 12: Aliens — Enemies and Allies]]'' (1995), ''[[Secrets of the Sisar Run]]'' ([[1997]]), ''[[Star Wars Trilogy Sourcebook, Special Edition]]'' (1997) and ''[[Geonosis and the Outer Rim Worlds]]'' ([[2004]]), three of which featured Carey on their writing teams. ''[[The New Jedi Order: Agents of Chaos II: Jedi Eclipse]]'' ([[2000]]) was the first novel in which Sriluur actually appeared. Most other appearances have been either brief glimpses of the planet, casual mentions, or, in the case of reference books, added little new information. ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' ([[2009]]) finally pinpointed Sriluur's location.

===Conflicting sources===
''Galaxy Guide 12: Aliens — Enemies and Allies''<ref name="GG12p" /> and ''Geonosis and the Outer Rim Worlds''<ref name="GATORWp" /> both state that a standard year on Sriluur consists of 270 days. This is contradicted by the ''Legacy Era Campaign Guide'', which claims the year has 295 days.<ref name="LECGp" /> Seeing as the ''Legacy Era Campaign Guide'' is the most recent source, this article assumes it to be correct.
